name: Tai-Kadai Family

formality.description: Tai-Kadai languages generally express formality through particles, pronouns of politeness, and register-specific vocabulary rather than inflectional changes. Thai and Lao have elaborate pronoun systems encoding social hierarchy, gender of speaker, and formality level.

gender.inclusiveGuidance: Tai-Kadai languages have no grammatical gender. Pronouns are generally gender-neutral, though some languages (e.g., Thai) have gendered politeness particles (ครับ/khrap for male speakers, ค่ะ/kha for female speakers) that are pragmatic rather than grammatical.

linguisticChallenges.tonalAccuracy: All major Tai-Kadai languages are tonal (typically 4–8 tones). Tone is lexically contrastive — the same syllable with different tones has completely different meanings. Romanized transcriptions require accurate tone diacritics. MT systems frequently produce tone errors.
linguisticChallenges.classifierSelection: Extensive classifier (measure word/numeral classifier) systems are universal in the family. Every noun has one or more associated classifiers used in counting, quantification, and reference. Using the wrong classifier is a clear non-native error.
linguisticChallenges.serialVerbConstructions: Serial verb constructions are the primary means of expressing complex events — multiple verbs are strung together without conjunctions or subordination. These sequences have specific ordering constraints and cannot be decomposed into separate clauses without losing meaning.
linguisticChallenges.noInflection: Tai-Kadai languages have virtually no inflectional morphology — no conjugation, declension, or agreement. Tense, aspect, and mood are expressed through particles and word order. MT systems may incorrectly generate inflected forms.
linguisticChallenges.wordBoundaries: Thai and Lao scripts do not use spaces between words, only between clauses or sentences. Word segmentation is a critical preprocessing challenge for MT. Even with Latin-script languages, compound words and collocations create boundary ambiguity.
linguisticChallenges.topicComment: Topic-comment structures are common, where the topic of a sentence is fronted regardless of its grammatical role. This pragmatic word order cannot be handled by rigid syntactic transformations.

notes: Family card for Tai-Kadai (~88 members). Covers Tai branch (Thai, Lao, Shan, Zhuang), Kam-Sui, Hlai, and other branches. Script is null because members use Thai, Lao, Tai Tham, New Tai Lue, Zhuang Latin, and other scripts.

regions.region: Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, Myanmar, southern China (Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou)
